title: Grateful Dead Live at Lane Community College on 1971-01-22
lineage: SBD > (unknown analog gens) > Cass > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Muddy audience tape of a raw early‑'70s show; despite lo‑fi sound the set delivers spirited Hard to Handle, Pig, Brokedown Palace and a lively Casey Jones opener.
ai_review.review: The recording is an audience capture on reused reel‑to‑reel tape that suffers from distortion, hiss and a weak drum mix, making it only fair to listen to without EQ work. Musically the performance is uneven – some reviewers find the jams uninspired while others praise Jerry’s solo on Hard to Handle, the bluesy Pig medley and the heartfelt Brokedown Palace – giving the show an overall mixed but historically interesting feel.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is average to good (≈3.5/5) while recording quality is poor to fair (≈2/5). Weighted by the 70 % show / 30 % recording split this yields an overall rating just above three stars.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Tape was recorded on a previously used reel‑to‑reel, resulting in muddy, distorted sound with noticeable hiss and a weak drum mix; some listeners improve it with EQ but overall clarity is limited.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The fragmentary tape captures a raw, psychedelic Warlocks‑era set; the band swings between loose improvisation and moments of tightness, giving an uneven but historically vivid flow.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His solo on Hard to Handle is highlighted – described as a train‑like lead that some listeners love despite the muddy mix.
band_member_comments.Phil: Mentioned for taking over the jam when the theme fell apart and for urging the band back into sync; his bass presence is noted but often buried in the tape.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s vocal on Casey Jones is described as “all in a tizzy,” indicating a lively rhythm‑guitar/vocal contribution.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey’s drumming is hard to hear due to the poor mix; one reviewer notes the sound board was turned up so loud it caused physical discomfort.
